Logic and ??

+

Logic, ??, and ?:

&& binds tighter than || and looser than the - comparisons; parenthesise when in doubt. ?? is null-coalescing, - not a truthiness fallback — it only substitutes when the left side is null/undefined, - so an empty string or 0 on the left is kept. + comparisons; parenthesise when in doubt. The three are distinct, and reaching + for the wrong one is the classic trap — || is the boolean + operator (it answers “is either truthy?”), so {t("{{nickname || name}}")} + outputs the text true, not a name. To fall back to a value, + use a coalesce: +

+ + + + + + + +
OperatorAnswersYields{t("{{nickname OP name}}")}, nickname: ""
||is either truthy?a booleanHi true
??is the left present? (non-null)a valueHi (keeps the "")
?:is the left truthy?a valueHi Ada
+

+ So ?? only substitutes on null/undefined (an empty string or 0 + on the left is kept), while ?: (Elvis) substitutes whenever the left is + falsy under MaxBars’ rule — the operator you want for a blank-or-missing fallback. + A boolean ||/&& left in output position is flagged by + flatbars lint --maxbars.
